items.q: At dynamic equilibrium, what is happening to the reactions?
items.correct: Forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; concentrations remain constant.
items.misconception: Both reactions stop because the system has reached balance.
items.random_wrong: The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.
items.why: The word 'equilibrium' connotes stillness, so students think reactions stop — they miss that equilibrium is dynamic at the particle level.

items.q: Maximum electrons in a p sub-shell:
items.why: Correct answer: 6. “10” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.
The answer examiners want is: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d⁶ 4s². “1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 4p⁶” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: How many electrons in a fully filled 3rd shell (n=3)?
items.why: Exact answer: 18. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.
